pre_flight_check.py.failing_input: the repo's own LIVE pre-flight (--pipeline all) on this tree: at least one gate FAILs, so the report's summary.fail > 0
pre_flight_check.py.verdict_location: the process exit code (1 when summary.fail > 0) AND the `summary` block of the --json report; consume with `wf_launch_gate_verdict.py preflight --report <pre_flight.json>`

wave_budget_tracker.py.failing_input: --budget-hr 0.1 against the repo's auto-discovered wave list: the tracker must DEFER waves and report remaining_hr < 0
wave_budget_tracker.py.verdict_location: NOT the exit code (0 on every path): the `remaining_hr` and `deferred_waves` fields of the --report-json report; consume with `wf_launch_gate_verdict.py budget --report <budget.json>`

per_wave_checklist.py.failing_input: a crafted pre-flight report with summary.fail=1 and a P0 blocker gate with status=FAIL, passed via --preflight
per_wave_checklist.py.verdict_location: NOT the exit code (0 on every path): the `preflight_fail_count` and `p0_blocker_gates[].status` fields of the --out JSON; consume with `wf_launch_gate_verdict.py checklist --report <per_wave.json>`

wf343c2_per_wave_check.py.failing_input: the same crafted pre-flight report (summary.fail=1, a P0 gate FAIL) via --preflight --preflight-live; --skip-live keeps the GPU/disk probes out of the measurement
wf343c2_per_wave_check.py.verdict_location: the process exit code (1 when any check FAILs) AND the `overall_status` / `checks[].status` of the --out JSON

wf343c3_data_quality_check.py.failing_input: a crafted loader CSV (one NaN pIC50 row) injected into the tool's own _load_binding_db by a generated driver, so ONE loader FAILs; the tool itself is run with --strict
wf343c3_data_quality_check.py.verdict_location: the process exit code (1 when a loader FAILs, or when --strict escalates a loader-level SKIP) AND the `loader_reports[].status` of the --out-dir report.json

abort_recovery.py.failing_input: a crafted failing train log carrying the OOM signature plus a checkpoint candidate that torch.load cannot read; --pattern OOM --metal Ru are both supplied (the log is the trigger artefact a wrapper greps for; the tool itself consumes the checkpoint)
abort_recovery.py.verdict_location: the process exit code (1 when `recovered` is false) AND the `recovered` / `verify` fields of the --report-json report

wf_launch_gate_verdict.py.failing_input: a crafted pre-flight report with summary.fail=1 (the shared verdict CONSUMER; a FAIL here is the expected behaviour)
wf_launch_gate_verdict.py.verdict_location: the process exit code (1 on FAIL) and the first stdout token; with --json the verdict is the `verdict` / `detail` fields
